55457.x: A breast ultrasound normally depends on a trained hand holding the probe, which keeps the exam inside the clinic. Catching something early is only possible if the screening actually happens.
NEOFORM and Hanseo University were named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for ONU, a clinician-connected home breast-screening system with guided ultrasound.

ONU judges ultrasound scan quality while the scan is still happening, the description says, so a lay user at home can produce clinician-reviewable breast images without operator training. It notes that five-year relative survival falls from 100 percent for localized breast cancer to 33.8 percent once disease is distant, yet routine screening is easy to postpone.

A circular smart-mirror display, a wireless linear-array probe and a charging dock guide preparation, probe positioning, scan direction and progress through visual and voice prompts, while ultrasound, motion, contact and position data are synchronized to evaluate handling stability, image quality and scan coverage during use. When incomplete areas are identified, the mirror guides location-specific rescanning before the session ends.

Powder-room placement links gel application to cleanup, and a modular architecture supports component-level replacement; the description says ONU extends breast-health management from isolated clinical visits to repeatable home participation while preserving mammography, professional interpretation and diagnosis.

NEXA was named a 2027 Honoree in Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MegaConnect, a rugged portable 5G hotspot.

Powered by FirstNet MegaRange and 5G+, MegaConnect is a rugged, portable 5G HPUE hotspot for enterprise and public-sector use. With 1.25W transmission power, the highest allowed in the U.S., it delivers stronger signal reach and up to twice the upload throughput of standard devices in challenging environments.

The device supports up to 64 Wi-Fi connections and runs with no battery for continuous use, and built with Qualcomm Snapdragon and certified for FirstNet Trusted, it meets high security standards for mission-critical communications.

Designed in partnership with AT&T and FirstNet and leveraging AT&T and FirstNet MegaRange technology, MegaConnect provides extended coverage and improved reliability over traditional hotspots, with a compact form factor significantly smaller than other HPUE solutions for mobile teams in remote or high-demand conditions.

55459.x: Taking the mechanical column out of the steering wheel frees the cockpit to be arranged in new ways, but the wheel still has to feel connected to the road. Recreating that feedback electronically is the engineering test.
Nexteer Automotive was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the High Mount Direct Drive Steer-by-Wire Handwheel Actuator (HMDD).

Nexteer's High Mount Direct Drive Handwheel Actuator (HMDD) is a steer-by-wire component that captures driver steering inputs and converts them into electronic commands for the roadwheels, delivering road-feedback torque through a direct-drive motor and advanced control software.

Its stationary-hub design keeps the center section fixed relative to the driver, enabling consistent positioning of the airbag, controls and future center-hub features, while the compact, high-mount packaging supports alternative cockpit architectures and greater interior design flexibility.

HMDD incorporates fault-tolerant controls, dual-path communications and software-defined steering calibration that can be updated throughout the vehicle lifecycle, and it is designed for integration across internal-combustion, hybrid and electric platforms, supporting 12V and 48V architectures and left- and right-hand-drive configurations.

55460.x: A fitness ring or a tiny sensor has to think for itself, stay connected and run for days on a sliver of a battery, all at once. Fitting that into a single low-power chip is the constraint.
Nordic Semiconductor was named a 2027 Honoree in Embedded Technologies at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the nRF54LM20B wireless System-on-Chip.

The nRF54LM20B is an ultra-low-power wireless System-on-Chip for battery-powered connected products that need secure connectivity and on-device intelligence, the description says. It combines a 128 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 application processor, a 128 MHz RISC-V coprocessor, Nordic's proprietary 128 MHz Axon Neural Processing Unit, 2 MB non-volatile memory, 512 KB RAM, embedded security, peripherals and a multiprotocol 2.4 GHz radio in one device.

The integrated architecture supports TensorFlow Lite inference on the NPU and compact Neuton models on the CPU at the same time, plus wireless operation across Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Channel Sounding, Bluetooth Mesh, Matter, Thread, Zigbee, Aliro and proprietary 2.4 GHz protocols.

The description says it suits earbuds, fitness bands and rings, voice-controlled remotes and speakers, smart-home sensors, medical and industrial sensors, and asset trackers, where local inference improves responsiveness, privacy, battery life and product size.

55461.x: Nuvell Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Food Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for NUVELL Plantein, an automated plant-protein appliance.

NUVELL Plantein is an AI-powered smart countertop platform that fully automates plant-protein production, the description says. It consolidates high-speed blending, thermal processing, filtration, liquid transfer, coagulation and mechanical pressing into a single hands-free workflow.

Its integrated electromechanical architecture combines sensor-driven control, Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) thermal compensation and mechanized pressing to turn raw ingredients directly into fresh plant milk or pressed tofu, removing manual straining and hot-liquid transfers.

A companion app supports remote control, recipe management and personalized nutrition tracking, while an auto-cleaning cycle simplifies maintenance; the description frames it as turning a fragmented, multi-stage process into one connected appliance.
Making plant milk or tofu at home means blending, boiling, straining and pressing, with hot liquid moved from pot to pot. The mess and the hot transfers are what keep most people from bothering.

55475.x: As companies turn loose fleets of AI agents, each one can reach for credentials and systems on its own. Keeping that authority in check, from outside the agent, is the safety question.
NVIDIA was named a 2027 Honoree in Cybersecurity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for NVIDIA OpenShell.

NVIDIA OpenShell is a secure runtime for AI agents that governs multi-agent fleets in production, the description says, enforcing access control, credential isolation and audit logging outside the agent, in the infrastructure layer beneath it.

Enforcement uses Landlock, a Linux kernel mandatory-access-control mechanism, layered with network, process and I/O confinement across six policy domains; every sandbox starts with zero permissions until a signed policy grants access. Credentials are scoped, injected at runtime and refreshed rather than held by the agent, sub-agents receive narrower, auditable authority than their parent, and denied actions convert into scoped approval workflows, while sandboxes reconnect and recover across process termination and model context limits.

The description says this lets security and platform teams move agents from pilot to production with policy-verified enforcement and a fleet-level audit trail, running unmodified across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and custom agents, and deploying on Kubernetes, Red Hat OpenShift and enterprise Linux.

NVIDIA was named a 2027 Honoree in Gaming & eSports at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the NVIDIA RTX Spark Superchip and Laptops.

NVIDIA RTX Spark is a superchip platform for slim Windows laptops and compact desktops, combining AI, graphics and general-purpose computing for local AI, content creation and gaming, the description says.

The superchip connects an NVIDIA Grace CPU with up to 20 cores and an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores through an NVLink C2C interconnect, sharing up to 128 GB of unified memory between CPU and GPU, while fifth-generation Tensor Cores support FP4 precision for up to one petaflop of AI compute, letting AI models and 3D scenes share memory rather than duplicate data across separate pools.

Running locally, the description says RTX Spark runs AI models with up to 120 billion parameters and one million tokens of context, renders 3D scenes over 90 GB, edits 12K video and plays AAA games at 1440p above 100 frames per second, with laptops as thin as 14 mm planned for fall 2026.

55478.x: Training the largest AI models has outgrown any single machine, so the work spreads across a rack full of them. How tightly that rack is wired together decides how much it can do.
NVIDIA was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is a rack-scale AI-computing system built on the third-generation NVIDIA MGX NVL72 rack design, integrating six new chips for agentic AI workloads, the description says.

The rack connects 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs across 18 compute trays and 9 NVLink switch trays, alongside ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs and Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches; each Rubin GPU includes up to 288 GB of HBM4, and sixth-generation NVLink delivers 3.6 TB/s per GPU and 260 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth per rack. A PCB midplane replaces the cabling, hoses and fans of prior compute trays, and the system is fully liquid-cooled at a 45C inlet.

Dynamic Max-Q power provisioning and Intelligent Power Smoothing, with 400 J of per-GPU energy storage, reclaim stranded power, and the description says NVIDIA Confidential Computing spans the rack while BlueField-4 DPUs add zero-trust security, with general availability in the second half of 2026.

It offers thin, flexible tactile sensor modules integrated with advanced optoelectronic sensing and real-time signal processing, enabling precise measurement of contact forces, pressure distribution and slip.

Ouster was named a 2027 Honoree in Embedded Technologies at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Ouster Rev8, a digital color lidar platform.

The Rev8 sensor is described as a next-generation digital color lidar platform for Physical AI across robotics, autonomous vehicles, industrial applications and smart infrastructure. It combines lidar ranging with color imaging in a single sensor, which the description says lets machines detect, classify and understand objects with greater accuracy across any environment.

Powered by Ouster's fourth-generation L4 silicon, Rev8 delivers high point-cloud density, doubled range performance and integrated color data while maintaining automotive-grade functional safety and cybersecurity standards.

By combining multiple sensing capabilities into one device, the description says it reduces system complexity while improving perception for applications that rely on accurate environmental understanding, from intelligent transportation systems to critical infrastructure.

55482.x: A creative workstation tends to sprout cables for drives, cards, screens and networking until the desk disappears. Pulling all of it into one hub is the tidy ideal.
PEXAR CO., LIMITED was named a 2027 Honoree in Computer Peripherals & Accessories at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Pexarbolt Ultra TBT5 Dock, a Thunderbolt 5 workstation hub.

The Pexarbolt Ultra TBT5 Dock is a Thunderbolt 5 workstation hub built for high-end creators and AI-assisted workflows, the description says. A 22-in-1 port matrix includes a Thunderbolt 5 host connection with 140W power delivery, downstream TB5 expansion, 10GbE networking, CFexpress Type B and SD/microSD UHS-II card readers, high-speed USB-C and USB-A ports, audio I/O, display output and an integrated M.2 NVMe slot for user-installed SSDs, while a 240W power architecture and active thermal management keep performance stable through rendering, large transfers and multi-display sessions.
A 5-inch full-color screen on the front shows live hardware status alongside the state of any AI sessions running on the connected machine.

A rotary dial lets users approve or reject risky AI operations directly on the device, and the description says a companion mobile app extends that same monitoring to a phone, even when no one is at the desk.

The description says it can also simulate match scenarios and deliver individualized performance insights and technical reports.
Powered by a dedicated AI chip, Aura is positioned as turning every training session into a personalized coaching experience aimed at accelerating skill development and performance.

Building on Shokz's open-ear bone conduction design, it is meant to offer greater convenience and long-term comfort, with intuitive controls and an easy-to-wear, age-friendly form factor.

Combined with personalized hearing fitting, a proprietary bone conduction driver, directional microphones and environmental noise reduction, the description says it enhances hearing clarity while reducing background noise.
With audio streaming, its use extends to everyday listening, helping users stay socially connected and reduce communication barriers.

55489.x: Rehabilitation progress is usually measured in a clinic, with a therapist and a goniometer, a visit at a time. Between those visits, how the exercises actually go is mostly invisible.
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Smart Motion Capture App for Rehabilitation (SMCAR).

SMCAR turns a standard iPhone or iPad running iOS 17 or later into a clinical-grade, markerless motion-capture system for remote rehabilitation. The description says it uses ARKit and a hybrid CNN-Transformer pose-estimation algorithm to track 22 body joints with under 15 degrees mean absolute error, and gives dual real-time feedback: a virtual avatar mirroring the patient's motion and live graphs of joint-angle changes.

A hybrid guidance system overlays the user's augmented-reality skeleton alongside an instructor video, adjusting playback speed to performance gaps. It automates active range of motion (AROM) measurements without clinician-administered goniometer tests, stores longitudinal performance data and supports standardized motor-impairment assessments such as the Fugl-Meyer.

By delivering laboratory-grade kinematic analysis on consumer devices with under 10ms rendering latency, the description says SMCAR widens access to precision neurorehabilitation, enabling continuous remote monitoring and adaptive exercise progression.

55500.x: HELIOS (Yoo hyeon Pacific Group Co., Ltd.), a supply-chain risk intelligence company led by CEO Antonio Kim, is speeding up its push into global markets with a dual-use strategy that covers both defense and industry. Founded in June 2023, the company builds on Kim's experience conducting risk research and entity verification at overseas sites. Instead of collecting as much open-source intelligence (OSINT) as possible, HELIOS delivers only facts confirmed through cross-verification. It began developing its platform in 2024, grew revenue 3.5 times from 2023 to 2025 without outside equity investment, and recorded cumulative U.S. exports of USD 43,500 from 2025 through the first half of 2026.

Risks involving Tier 3 and lower suppliers, which are difficult to monitor through companies' internal systems, have become a major concern for global manufacturers and defense contractors. A 2025 report by the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that even the U.S. Department of Defense had identified fewer than 10% of the F-35's lower-tier suppliers. Kim said global defense contractors such as Lockheed Martin have visibility into their Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers but lack insight into the sourcing networks of their Tier 3 and Tier 4 suppliers, driving demand for supplier verification. Two deadlines add to the pressure: the second phase of U.S. National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) Section 805 takes effect in June 2027, and EU supply-chain due diligence rules apply from 2029. Exporters and defense supply-chain participants in Korea and abroad will increasingly need to account for their lower-tier suppliers.

HELIOS runs two products on one analysis engine: HELIOS ATLAS for industry and HELIOS AEGIS for defense and public-sector closed networks. ATLAS combines external risk information with the supplier lists that manufacturers and exporters already hold, continuously monitoring Tier 3 and lower suppliers for links to sanctioned or restricted entities, single-country dependence, unclear ownership, counterfeit parts and disruption signals. AEGIS is installed on closed networks and provides security briefings that cover Korean Peninsula security and global geopolitical risks, along with supply alerts for strategic materials such as rare earths.

To reduce false alarms, HELIOS classifies a single-source signal as "unconfirmed" and marks a finding as "confirmed" only when two or more independent signals agree. It cross-checks public signals such as multilingual news in Korean and Chinese, filings, ship and flight tracks, satellite heat spots and raw-material prices. When needed, it also conducts on-site verification (ground truth) through its field partner network in Asia. By operating its own servers and designing for closed networks, HELIOS blocks customer data from leaving the customer's environment. It keeps its past judgments unedited and later compares them with actual outcomes, and it offers an eight-week free pilot using the suppliers of a single product line as a sample.

HELIOS operates in two business segments: B2B (Business to Business) and B2G (Business to Government). In the B2G segment, it is providing regular briefings to two defense and public-sector users on a pilot basis. It provides defense intelligence agencies and export-related public agencies with analysis of threat information on the Korean Peninsula and in East Asia, as well as reports forecasting imported raw-material price changes based on geopolitical risk.

In B2B, HELIOS supplies or targets defense prime contractors and their Tier 2 and Tier 3 suppliers; battery, semiconductor and electronic-component makers and exporters; and consulting and law firms conducting export-control and environmental, social and governance (ESG) due diligence. It has recently been working with battery-related companies. In addition to Korea, the company is targeting North America and Europe. HELIOS's attendance at the International Defence Industry Exhibition (MSPO) in Poland also highlighted strong European demand for OSINT-based supply-chain intelligence.

Operating through its U.S. entity, HELIOS Security Solutions LLC, the company has already secured some U.S. defense and public-sector partners and is preparing to enter the U.S. market. In Taiwan, whose companies sell deep into U.S. AI, semiconductor and defense supply chains, HELIOS is seeking to launch an eight-week free pilot with component makers and electronics manufacturing services (EMS) firms and to cooperate with local research and consulting partners.

In 2026, HELIOS was selected for Gyeonggi Province's global startup commercialization program and the Korean Intellectual Property Office's IP Narae program. Kim said that Pangyo's concentration of AI, semiconductor and software companies and the R&D teams of defense and electronics firms, combined with its startup ecosystem, lets the company quickly gauge demand at home and abroad and meet potential customers and technical talent nearby. He added that the global support programs of the Gyeonggido Business & Science Accelerator (GBSA), and access to public agencies in Seoul and the capital area and to Incheon International Airport, are strengths in preparing for overseas business.

Beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026, HELIOS plans to step up pilots with Korean manufacturers and development of a tool that checks ownership structure and sanctions exposure in response to NDAA Section 805. In December 2026, it plans to file a Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) international application for its core patent (Korean application 10-2025-0198504). In January 2027, it will unveil ATLAS in the Gyeonggi pavilion at CES 2027 Eureka Park in Las Vegas and pursue its first seed round of about KRW 500 million (about USD 372,000). The company targets entry into the U.S. defense market in 2026 and expansion in 2027 into defense and semiconductor supply-chain markets in Korea, the U.S. and East Asia.

55506.x: A long car fighting its way into a tight parking spot or a narrow alley is held back by how sharply its wheels can turn. Steering all four wheels independently rewrites what a vehicle can do in a small space.
Hyundai Mobis was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Horizontal 4-Wheel Independent Steering System (4WiS).

Horizontal 4-Wheel Independent Steering (4WiS) is a next-generation steering system that independently controls all four wheels for maneuverability, stability and motion control. It combines horizontally packaged steering actuators with an independent rack-bar architecture, enabling software-defined optimization of vehicle dynamics: at low speeds it significantly reduces turning radius for maneuverability, and at high speeds it enhances stability, handling and driving confidence.

A key innovation is its horizontal actuator packaging, which enables integration into mass-production platforms for both internal-combustion and electric vehicles, while its fail-operational architecture maintains steering even if one or more actuators fail.

More than a steering technology, Horizontal 4WiS is a scalable mobility platform that integrates steering, software-defined motion control and fail-operational safety as a foundation for future autonomous and software-defined mobility.

55507.x: A fixed screen in a car claims its slice of the dashboard forever, whether or not anyone is using it. A display that moves into reach only when wanted, and tucks away when not, rethinks the whole cabin.
Hyundai Mobis received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in In-Vehicle Entertainment at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the M-Moving Display, a space-adaptive display platform.

M-Moving Display is billed as the world's first space-adaptive display platform, dynamically adapting its position and interaction area to user needs and vehicle usage scenarios. Unlike conventional displays that permanently occupy cabin space, it integrates into the cockpit architecture and provides digital interaction only when required.

The platform combines a flexible display with a proprietary hidden magnetic motion architecture that enables movement across complex freeform cockpit surfaces while maintaining direct-touch usability.

Rather than requiring the interior to accommodate a fixed display, M-Moving lets the display itself adapt to available space, user preferences, interaction requirements and cabin configurations, enabling cleaner interiors, improved space utilization, personalized experiences and greater design freedom for OEMs.

55508.x: In a rollover, the greatest danger is being thrown through an opening in the car, and the sunroof is the one most airbags never cover. Those seconds of tumbling are where protection has been missing.
Hyundai Mobis was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for its Roof Airbag (RAB) for rollover ejection prevention.

The description calls it the world's first airbag system designed to protect occupants during rollover crashes. Hidden within the sunroof assembly, it deploys in roughly 80 milliseconds to fully cover the sunroof opening and create a barrier between occupants and the outside.

It helps reduce head injuries from impacts with roof glass, vehicle structures and external objects during a rollover, and helps keep shattered glass out of the cabin. Because occupant ejection is one of the deadliest consequences of rollovers, the description says the Roof Airbag helps prevent occupants from being thrown through the sunroof opening, keeping them inside the vehicle.
Seamlessly integrated into the existing sunroof structure, it preserves normal sunroof function while adding the safety performance.

With a Flat Cabinet and Hidden Hinge, the tower delivers premium performance in a space-conscious design.

55515.x: Servers that handle large workloads can run out of memory slots long before they run out of data to hold. Packing more capacity into each slot is one way around that.
Samsung Electronics was named a 2027 Honoree in Computer Hardware & Components at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for DDR5 RDIMM 512GB (32Gb).

Samsung's 512GB DDR5 RDIMM is a high-capacity server memory module built with advanced 32Gb DRAM technology, designed for high-performance computing and next-generation data centers. Using 32Gb DRAM, it delivers 512GB of capacity with a four-layer stacking structure, compared to eight layers in conventional 16Gb DRAM-based modules. The simplified design is meant to reduce packaging complexity while supporting greater design flexibility.

In a server with 16 memory channels at 1DPC, 512GB RDIMMs can provide up to 8TB of memory capacity, twice the maximum 4TB capacity achievable with 256GB RDIMMs. DPC stands for DIMMs per memory channel, and 1DPC means one. The module also consumes up to 15% less power than conventional 16Gb DRAM-based 512GB RDIMMs, which is billed as helping reduce power consumption and cooling demands in data centers.

It supports memory-intensive workloads such as generative AI training, machine learning and enterprise big data analytics, and is billed as helping improve data center operational efficiency and reduce TCO.

55519.x: Heart failure often worsens quietly between appointments, and by the time it shows, the patient is back in the hospital. If a few seconds of speech could flag the decline early, help could come sooner.
a.cure was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Heart to Voice, a voice-based AI for early heart failure detection.

Heart to Voice (H2V) is a first-of-its-kind voice-based AI monitoring solution that detects heart failure worsening from a minimum of 10 seconds of speech, consolidating nine clinical heart failure indicators into a unified Heart Failure Composite Score that estimates clinically defined heart failure status directly from voice.

Heart failure patients frequently deteriorate between hospital visits, driving repeated readmissions, high mortality and missed opportunities for timely intervention, while existing monitoring approaches rely on wearable devices, dedicated sensors or indirect physiological measurements that are difficult to use consistently, particularly for older adults.

By tracking personalized changes over time, H2V enables earlier identification of worsening and provides interpretable health information and actionable care guidance, aiming to make heart failure monitoring more accessible and scalable beyond traditional healthcare settings.

55523.x: A security camera that captures faces and license plates also captures a target for anyone who breaks in. The safest record is the one that was never created.
Advance Robotics Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Cybersecurity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for QRNG-RAW, a RAW-based privacy camera module.

QRNG-RAW is a camera module that removes personal data before an image is formed, the description says. Positioned between the image sensor and the ISP, an AI detection layer identifies faces, license plates, bodies and documents directly in 12-bit RAW data, before any viewable image exists.

In the default track, a quantum random number generator (NIST SP 800-90A/B compliant) irreversibly overwrites those regions through triple destruction, quantum-noise substitution, bit-depth reduction and spatial degradation, so no original exists to leak, while background context remains intact for security monitoring. In a legally gated second track, regions are instead encrypted with quantum-generated AES-256 keys stored in a hardware security module and automatically destroyed on expiry, with every access recorded in a tamper-evident audit log.

The description says all processing runs on-device in real time at 1080p 30 fps, and the module integrates into CCTV, service robots, elevators, hospitals and vehicles without changes to existing video-management systems.

Coordinated swarm coverage targets more than 65 percent higher coverage efficiency than a single drone, more than 45 percent lifecycle savings, and replacing up to five conventional units. One operator carries the swarm to the site and deploys it within minutes.
The description notes SkyRanger is at prototype stage, with its cooperative navigation system in development.

55526.x: A brain tumor shows up as dozens of flat scan slices that a surgeon has to assemble into a shape in their head, while the patient is left guessing at what is at stake. Seeing it whole, in one picture, helps both sides of that conversation.
AI:BLE Insight was named a 2027 Honoree in Products in Support of Human Security for All at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MedNeuro3D NeuroVista, an AI neuro-oncology collaboration platform.

MedNeuro3D NeuroVista is a first-of-its-kind AI-assisted 3D neuro-oncology platform that turns scattered brain images into one shared clinical case for clinicians, patients and families. In brain-tumor care, clinicians must mentally reconstruct the relationships among tumor, vessels and neural pathways from dozens of 2D slices, while patients and families struggle to understand what is affected and what must be protected.

NeuroVista assembles multimodal MRI and CT into a single interactive 3D case, connecting pre-operative review, post-operative comparison and remote consultation in one continuous context. Clinicians get a detailed view in which every finding can be traced back to the source images, and patients get a simplified view they can actually follow. Running in a standard browser with no dedicated workstation, it fits existing PACS workflows.
AI does not replace clinical judgment; NeuroVista exists so that the clinician's explanation becomes clearer and the patient's questions and choices are better respected.

55529.x: Remembering several pills a day is hard enough, and harder for someone who lives alone and does not use a smartphone. A reminder that works on an ordinary phone would reach people that apps leave out.
GASIAN was named a 2027 Honoree in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for DEFI Care Call — The Smart Pillbox That Calls You.

DEFI Care Call is built for seniors who own no smartphone, manage five or more daily medications and live alone. When a user misses an evening pill, DEFI notices, calls the user's phone and asks whether the dose was taken, offering to call back in ten minutes. If the dose is still missed, a family member gets the next call, with a same-day report.
A 14-slot smart pillbox confirms each retrieval with dual IR and Hall-effect sensors, and a conversational AI escalates every missed dose until it is resolved or a family member knows.

55533.x: An induction cooktop is fast and clean but refuses to heat a glass or ceramic pot, while a hot coil runs too fierce to pair with it. Combining both in one zone would end the trade-off between speed and what you can put on it.
Graphene Square was named a 2027 Honoree at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Graphene Induction Hybrid Cooker.

The graphene induction hybrid cooker is billed as the world's first cookware that can simultaneously use induction and Joule heating in a single cooking zone. A conventional induction range needs special cookware that turns a high-frequency magnetic field into an internal current that generates heat through electrical resistance, so non-magnetic metals or ceramic and glass cookware cannot be used, while heating coils are usually bulky and locally too hot, above 900 degrees Celsius, to combine vertically with induction heating.
The cooker uses a transparent graphene film as a Joule heating component that does not interfere with induction, thanks to its thickness and transparency.

The 1 nm thick 3-layer graphene can be heated up to 500 degrees Celsius, and its mid-infrared radiation resonates with the typical molecular vibrational energy of food components (2 to 5 um), resulting in 30 percent improved energy efficiency.

SOFTPV Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SOLANE, a road- and path-integrated guidance module.

SOLANE converts passive lane markings into solar-powered, machine-readable infrastructure. Built on SOFTPV's 1 mm-class three-dimensional SOFTCELL platform, each unit harvests solar energy by day and stores it in an onboard battery; when ambient light falls below a set threshold, such as at night or in rain and fog, it automatically powers color-adjustable LEDs through prism optics to create a uniform illuminated lane surface for boundaries, directions, hazards and traffic instructions.

Independently of its lighting, the description says SOLANE transmits positional, environmental and operating data at scheduled intervals or in response to vehicle-passage events, supplementing onboard perception for connected vehicles and mobile robots.

Its modular, replaceable architecture supports roads, airports, logistics facilities, parking areas, bicycle lanes and pedestrian paths while reducing external power wiring and routine battery replacement.

AX-Guard is a distributed EV fire detection and underbody cooling infrastructure for smart-city, smart-venue and shared parking ecosystems. Each designated EV bay receives a floor-mounted node combining active off-gas sensing, optical temperature sensing, Edge AI cross-validation, local valve control and an underbody sprinkler.

Internal validation recorded precursor detection within 3 seconds, actuation within 5 seconds and a false-positive rate below 0.5%. Each node operates locally during network outages while reporting bay-level status to a centralized web dashboard.
More than 220 L/min is directed toward the battery pack to slow thermal escalation, while perimeter nozzles form a water curtain that limits propagation.
The anchor-bolted, low-profile retrofit design allows municipalities and property operators to protect selected EV bays incrementally without reconstructing the entire parking facility.

55557.x: Swallowing a handful of supplement pills gets harder with age, and much of what is swallowed never fully absorbs. A thin film that dissolves in the mouth, tuned to the body's own readings, sidesteps both problems.
Top Table Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for IINK_nutriflex, an AI-driven adaptive nutrition platform.

IINK_nutriflex is billed as the world's first AI-driven 5D Adaptive Manufacturing platform fabricating hyper-personalized Oral Dissolving Films (ODFs). A proprietary AI engine analyzes real-time biometric and metabolic data to compute precise formulations, establishing a predictive foundation to counteract biological aging and optimize cellular health at every life stage.

Moving beyond 3D and 4D printing, the platform pioneers 5D adaptive manufacturing, integrating AI data into the micro-fluidic loop for instant customization and shifting medical nutrition from labs into an accessible home appliance. Using advanced micro-layering, it encapsulates dynamic formulations into a water-free matrix whose direct mucosal pathway bypasses the aging gastrointestinal tract to elevate bioavailability to 95 percent, removing physical swallowing barriers (dysphagia).
Scaling into premium senior living and smart homes, IINK_nutriflex establishes a new paradigm in software-controlled preventive nutrition, delivering a barrier-free, independent longevity ecosystem.

55558.x: A face or a fingerprint at the door is only as trustworthy as the system's ability to tell a real one from a fake. A photo, a mask or a molded print can stand in for the genuine article.
UNION biometrics Co., Ltd. received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Cybersecurity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for UBio-X LiveGuard, a multimodal biometric security device.

The description calls LiveGuard a world-first device that combines face and fingerprint anti-spoofing with fully on-device AI. It is built to detect sophisticated attacks, including deepfakes, 3D masks, replayed images and silicone or gelatin fingerprints, while authenticating legitimate users in under a second.

Unlike server-dependent systems, it runs AI inference, liveness detection, biometric matching and access decisions locally, staying fully operational offline, with fingerprint identification up to 1:100,000. The description frames this as shifting access control from matching an identity to proving that a live human is present.
Its anti-spoofing is backed by U.S. and Korean patents and independently validated through KISA K-NBTC Class 1 testing, along with face and fingerprint algorithm performance certifications.

55559.x: Safety sensors for the home tend to come one function per device and one setup per room, leaving gaps between them. And the rooms that most need watching are the ones where a camera is least welcome.
uniuni corp received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Smart Home at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SAVVY SPACE AI, a privacy-preserving smart-home safety device.

SAVVY SPACE AI automatically adapts to the room it is installed in. Using non-identifying spatial, acoustic, occupancy, environmental and event signals, the description says it recognizes whether it is operating in a bathroom, bedroom, living room, kitchen, hallway or home-care space, and its Space-Adaptive AI then recommends, and can automatically apply, the detection functions, sensitivity levels and alert settings appropriate to that room.

Depending on the location, it can detect falls, fainting, abnormal inactivity, prolonged occupancy, smoke, fire, air-quality deterioration, screams, violence and emergency-button events, and authorized household members or caregivers can review and modify the settings.

The device supports ceiling or wall mounting, wired power, Wi-Fi or Ethernet connectivity and event-based alerts, and the description says it uses no RGB video, facial recognition or identifiable imagery.

55560.x: Tracking progress on a construction site usually means photos, measurements and someone walking the floor with a checklist. Flat images rarely show how far along the work really is.
UPSIGHT CO., LTD. was named a 2027 Honoree in Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for UPSIGHT Reconstruct, an AI spatial progress verification tool.

UPSIGHT Reconstruct turns an ordinary phone-video walk-through into a measurable 3D model of a construction site, with no LiDAR, survey crew or special hardware. A site engineer records while walking the site, and the description says the system filters the frames, rebuilds the jobsite in 3D within two to four hours, and aligns it to the drawings and schedule.
From there, teams can measure distances and dimensions, compare planned against actual progress, and locate issues in spatial context rather than in flat photos.

In internal validation cited in the description, it reached a 0.945 percent distance error over 100 meters from ordinary mobile video, at roughly USD 2 of graphics compute per reconstruction, compared with the USD 50,000 to 60,000 of a LiDAR rig.

55561.x: Firefighters who enter a smoke-filled ship move through spaces where almost nothing is visible. What little they can see comes through the narrow shield of a breathing mask.

VIRNECT was named a 2027 Honoree in three categories, XR & Spatial Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and Products in Support of Human Security for All, at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for VisionX Marine, an optical see-through augmented-reality module.

VisionX Marine retrofits onto an existing self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) full-face mask by replacing only the visor, meaning the front shield, and the upper visor holder, while the mask body and face-seal geometry stay unchanged.

The display pairs two 0.6-inch micro-OLED panels, each at 1920 x 1080 RGB resolution with a 44-degree field of view, with near-eye optical assemblies. Because the architecture is optical see-through, the wearer looks at the floor and surroundings directly through the shield while digital content is laid over the view.
Only the optical assemblies stay inside the mask. The processor and battery sit in an external top module, which moves the main heat sources out of the sealed mask volume.
For positioning inside GPS-denied ship interiors, the system fuses camera-based Visual-Inertial Odometry with six-degree-of-freedom IMU dead reckoning, targeting sub-1-meter RMS accuracy.

55562.x: Fires and other hazards in forests, ports and along coastlines are easiest to handle when someone spots them early. Watching that much open ground around the clock is the hard part.
VisionCore was named a 2027 Honoree in Products in Support of Human Security for All at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for CamBOT Thermal Guard.

CamBOT Thermal Guard is a long-range thermal and visible-light surveillance system designed to help operators detect fires, heat-related hazards and other threats earlier across large outdoor areas. It combines thermal sensing, a 4 MP visible-light camera with 56× optical zoom, motorized pan-tilt control and AI-based event analysis in one platform.
Thermal imaging supports detection in darkness, smoke, fog, haze and backlighting, while the visible channel provides detailed verification.
The system can classify people and vehicles, support vessel detection, identify heat or early fire events, issue alerts and track targets.

Designed for forests, ports, airports, utilities, railways, industrial sites, coastlines and critical infrastructure, CamBOT Thermal Guard connects early hazard detection with remote verification and operator response from a control center.

55563.x: Many electrical fires begin with an arc fault, a small hidden spark inside wiring that a standard breaker can miss. By the time the damage shows, the fire may already have started.
VisionTech Corporation was named a 2027 Honoree in Products in Support of Human Security for All at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for VESI Arc-Guard, an intelligent arc-fault circuit breaker.

VESI Arc-Guard aims to prevent electrical fires and shocks while keeping power on. The description says it pairs proprietary leakage current-limiting technology with embedded edge AI, guiding hazardous leakage current through internal bypass pathways under high-humidity or submerged conditions so line voltage holds without a shock hazard.

Its on-device AI samples microsecond-level waveforms for real-time arc-fault detection and a four-stage safety classification of Safe, Caution, Warning and Danger. Rather than trip on every signal, the description says the AI validates whether tripping is needed and executes it only when a hazardous arc is confirmed, reducing false alarms while still acting on real hazards.

The system also detects degradation patterns and calculates Remaining Useful Life, and through edge and cloud connectivity it lets administrators monitor health and carry out predictive maintenance from a PC or mobile device.

55564.x: Riding a bus or finding the right counter in a public building takes practice, and practicing in the real world carries risks for people still learning. A safe place to repeat those situations gives them room to learn.
VRISVR was named a 2027 Honoree in EdTech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for DoItDoIt AI: AI-XR Adaptive Training Solution for Special Education.

DoItDoIt AI is an AI-powered extended reality (XR) adaptive training solution designed to foster independent living and social skills for individuals with developmental disabilities. The system delivers immersive, curriculum-aligned virtual simulations of everyday scenarios, such as using public transportation and community facilities, within safe, repeatable environments.

During training, the platform captures high-frequency behavioral data, including head movement patterns, gaze metrics and response times. A proprietary vertical AI model processes these behavioral and performance logs to objectively assess adaptive capabilities.

An integrated Agentic AI dynamically adjusts scenario difficulty and recommends tailored learning pathways, while automatically generating clinical and educational progress reports for teachers and caregivers via a centralized web dashboard.

55565.x: A passing thought is easy to lose before there is a chance to write it down. Speaking it aloud is quicker, but not always something to do out loud in company.
Vtouch, Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Fashion Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for WIZPR RING V2, a voice-input smart ring.

The 3-gram ring pairs a jewelry-inspired look with a private wellness feature, built around a seamless silicone unibody with interchangeable titanium covers in gold and rose-gold. To use it, the wearer brings it close to the lips and speaks, with no wake word or push-to-talk button.

Its NearVAD near-field voice detection focuses on intentional speech while playing down surrounding noise, and a feature called WIZPR Vibe lets users voice-type in compatible apps without taking out a phone. Across the day they can quietly capture thoughts and feelings.

Each evening, an AI-guided reflection turns those moments into a first-person journal in the user's own words. EDA, PPG and motion signals add context for wellness trends, with the sensor analysis running on the paired phone. The description lists up to two days of battery life and IPX7 water resistance.

55566.x: A self-driving system is usually as good as the day it was deployed, and no better. A road it has never seen, whether a new city, odd weather or an unfamiliar object, is where that limit shows.
Vueron Technology was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for X Prospector, a self-evolving multi-sensor perception platform.

The description notes that autonomous-driving perception typically freezes at deployment, leaving new conditions as on-road blind spots, a gap it links to more than 800 crashes reported to NHTSA's Standing General Order and clustered in exactly those edge cases. X Prospector is built to break that stagnation.

A synchronized LiDAR, camera and radar rig collects real-road data while Vueron's sensor-agnostic software runs at the edge with about 50-millisecond inference. When the vehicle enters Wi-Fi coverage, high-value data uploads on its own to a back end called X Factory for 3D auto-labeling, scenario mining and retraining, and the improved models redeploy straight back to the vehicle.

The result the description claims is accuracy that compounds with every mile driven rather than every software release. The X Prospector Console pulls perception, route and performance views into one screen, while unmanned auto-labeling removes what the company calls the largest recurring cost in AV development.

55567.x: A modern factory already runs on many systems, each tracking its own slice of the operation. The problem is that they rarely speak the same language, so joining the picture still falls to people.
WACE Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for VEXPLOR Suite, a manufacturing AI operating system with safety-graded autonomy.

VEXPLOR Suite sets out to unify factory operations into a single system. The description notes that most plants already own MES, ERP, sensors and dashboards, yet each speaks a different language, leaving engineers to chase quality problems by hand and AI stuck in pilots for lack of trust on live lines.

It standardizes plant data into more than 834 tables and 311 ontology relations, grounds every AI answer in that ontology so it is traceable rather than a black-box guess, and hands control to AI one verified safety level at a time, from read-only to supervised execution. Six integrated modules cover sensing, decision and execution.
According to the description, it runs at more than 20 manufacturing sites, and at one site hourly output rose more than 20 percent while process defects fell 26 percent.

55569.x: A blood test on an animal usually means restraint, a shaved patch and a needle. For an anxious pet, the handling can be as hard as the result is useful.
Wavena was named a 2027 Honoree in Pet & Animal Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Wavet, a non-invasive veterinary diagnostic AI platform.

Wavet estimates comprehensive blood chemistry panels from a standard 30-second animal ECG, with no needle, fur shaving or sedation. The description says its deep-learning model, adapted from a foundation model validated on more than 3.7 million clinical records, decodes fine cardiac electrophysiological signatures into systemic biomarker profiles.

The platform integrates through an authorized SDK with AliveCor's FDA-cleared portable ECG hardware. From that single reading it screens hematology such as WBC and hemoglobin, renal indices including BUN and creatinine, electrolytes, liver and nutritional markers, and glucose.
The intent, according to the description, is immediate and stress-free screening that supports timely treatment and remote tele-triage across veterinary clinics and homes.

55570.x: Most waste plastic still ends up burned or buried, in part because sorting and cleaning it for reuse is slow and costly. Mixed and dirty streams are the ones recyclers would rather not touch.

WES-Tec Global was named a 2027 Honoree in Energy Transition & Sustainability at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the REVOCLE AI System, a real-time waste-plastic analysis and automated processing system.

REVOCLE AI is an AI sensor-based automated control system offered as an alternative to incinerating waste plastic, which the description says reduces the related pollution and cost while removing the need for complex washing and sorting.

At the input stage it identifies the resin types, proportions and weight of incoming waste plastics, then calculates the lowest temperature needed for molding and automatically sets the melting unit to it. Integrated with a system that converts processed plastic into high-strength construction blocks (ECO-C CUBE), the description frames it as a circular solution.

The system can handle a wide range of materials, including common waste plastics, marine debris such as discarded fishing nets and buoys, and multilayer packaging, and the description says it was developed as a global alternative for waste-plastic treatment and sustainable recycling.

55571.x: A walker steadies someone on their feet, but it leaves the job of spotting danger to the person using it. A curb or a pothole still has to be seen in time.
HL Klemove was named a 2027 Honoree in two categories, Digital Health and Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility, at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Walkain.

Named for the idea of "Walk Again," Walkain is built for older adults and people with mobility challenges, and the description casts it as a shift from a passive aid to an active safety companion. It monitors both the user and the surroundings as a kind of digital guardian.

Using time-of-flight sensors, it detects hazards such as stairs, curbs, potholes and edges, then responds with timely alerts and braking assistance. Rather than only reacting once danger is present, the description says it works to anticipate risks before a situation escalates.
By combining hazard awareness, proactive intervention and digital health support, Walkain is intended to help users walk with more confidence and independence.

55572.x: A brake that drags even slightly when it should be off quietly steals range from an electric car and grinds out fine dust. Cutting that residual friction to almost nothing frees both the battery and the air.
HL Mando was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the HyperMotion Caliper Brake.

HyperMotion is a next-generation Caliper Motion Control technology developed to meet the Zero Drag requirements of electrified vehicles. The guide support structure and load transfer path are optimized for the increased weight and center-of-gravity shift of large MoC and EMB actuators, minimizing guide pin bending deformation while maintaining dynamic clearance and caliper centering, which reduces residual drag and improves braking response.
HyperMotion also enables a premium, monoblock-level exterior through a non-exposed guide structure, while providing a scalable architecture for future EMB platforms.

It reduces non-braking drag from 3 Nm to just 0.1 Nm, delivering about 4 additional miles of EV range per charge through improved energy efficiency and up to a 34 percent reduction in fine particulate emissions from brake wear.

55573.x: A warning light on the dash tells a driver that something is wrong, but not what, how urgent, or what to do about it. Having the car explain itself in plain words, before the light even comes on, is a different relationship with the machine.
HL Mando was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MiCOSA i-Butler, an onboard conversational AI assistant.

i-Butler is an onboard conversational AI assistant that predicts vehicle health from sensor, driving and environmental data, then explains its findings in plain language. Its hybrid architecture combines a 2.3-billion-parameter onboard multimodal model with a cloud-based LLM, keeping essential functions offline and responding in about 300 milliseconds.

AI-powered Prognostics and Health Management detects early signs of degradation in brake, tire, battery and steering systems up to 1,000 miles before a predicted fault and well before a warning light appears, then explains the likely cause, risk level, when service is needed and the recommended action at a level suited to each user. Selected functions, including drive-mode selection and cabin ventilation, can be controlled by voice.

During autonomous operation, i-Butler uses In2itive Twin visualization to explain vehicle behavior and the control responses behind it, and in emergencies it recommends next steps and, with user consent, initiates contact with emergency services and insurance providers.

55574.x: A car's driving, braking, steering and suspension have always been separate systems bolted around the frame. Packing all four into one corner module rethinks how a vehicle is built and how it can move.
HL Mando was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for motionXrite, an integrated chassis module.

motionXrite is a next-generation chassis system that integrates drive, braking, steering and suspension into a single module, and HL Mando has filed trademark applications for it in Korea, China, Europe and the United States.

Designed for vehicles and other mobility applications, it is a modular product that can be installed using a simple mounting interface, combining the four essential chassis functions in one unit. Independent drive, braking and steering control at each wheel enables not only forward, reverse and turning movements but also sideways driving, diagonal driving and turn-in-place rotation.
With its high maneuverability and modular architecture, motionXrite can be adapted to a wide range of vehicles and mobility platforms while increasing design freedom and improving space utilization.

55575.x: A crew working far from any outlet still needs reliable power, and a roaring generator gives away their position and chokes the air. Silent, emission-free power carried on the back changes what is possible off-grid.
HOGREENAIR CO., LTD. was named a 2027 Honoree in Energy Transition & Sustainability at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for HydroPack Pro, a wearable backpack hydrogen fuel cell power system.

The Backpack Hydrogen Fuel Cell Powerpack is an AI-driven, dual-fuel portable power system for off-grid operations and defense missions. Powered by a 1.2 kW fuel cell stack and a 48V buffer battery, it features an interchangeable storage system supporting either a 9.3 L (350 bar) compressed gas cylinder or a 10 L cryogenic liquid hydrogen tank.
Integrated Edge-AI continually predicts fuel consumption and optimizes power distribution based on connected loads.

Delivering silent, zero-emission electricity with field-swappable tanks, the multi-fuel powerpack provides extended, reliable energy for tactical communications, UAV charging and emergency response without carbon emissions.

55576.x: A brand pays a creator for views and only finds out afterward what actually sold, if anything. Funding the marketing on the revenue it produces, not the audience it reaches, flips that bet.
Hyperstar Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Hyperstar AI, a revenue AI agent for creator commerce.

Hyperstar AI funds creator marketing on revenue instead of reach. Brands buy views and followers, then learn what sold after the budget is spent, and analytics tools can describe that gap but cannot close the learning loop, because a system that only observes campaigns cannot connect its decisions to the money produced.

Hyperstar owns the loop: it forecasts the revenue a creator will generate, turns one video into 36 ad variations, runs the Meta media buy against a cost-per-click ceiling, then reconciles every forecast against settled transactions from six commerce platforms, refunds deducted, and retrains on the residual error. Because the agent executes its predicted campaign, each outcome becomes a training signal rather than a report, and the model has been reconciled against settled revenue in 37 commercial campaigns.
The result is a marketing system where verified revenue, not audience size or budget, decides where money goes.

55578.x: The record of a historic building often survives only as fragile hand-drawn plans. Turning those drawings into something a restoration crew can build from has long been slow, specialist work.
WIZCORE, Inc. received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Art Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for TWArch Master, an AI agent for architectural heritage restoration.

TWArch Master converts hand-drawn historical architectural drawings into construction-ready parametric 3D models. The description notes that restoration has conventionally required months of fragmented work across historians, structural engineers and CAD drafters, with no single tool linking historical records to a buildable output.

Built on a trained object-recognition model, it detects and classifies structural components from scanned drawings, converts them into editable 2D and 3D CAD objects, and allows real-time design changes through natural language. The description credits this with speeding restoration workflows by up to 60 times and cutting up to 90 percent of material waste through digital pre-simulation.

According to the description, the system is backed by a registered patent and three acknowledged research papers, and has been used to virtually restore a lost heritage site from historical drawings and ruins.

55579.x: A single prompt can conjure an image, but it hands the artist a finished picture they had little say in. Keeping control at each stage of the drawing is what a working illustrator actually needs.
Ys HUB Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence and Imaging at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for GlimNavi, an AI-assisted production environment for artists.

GlimNavi is an AI-assisted production environment for illustrators, comic and webtoon artists and visual content studios. It provides art-specific tools for pose and scene composition, sketch-to-line-art conversion, reference-guided coloring, 3D-to-illustrated background generation, camera-angle adjustment and visual refinement, and rather than relying on a single prompt to produce a finished image, creators select and control AI operations for individual production stages, reusing character, style, pose and visual references throughout the workflow.
For pose creation, a sensor-equipped physical mannequin can synchronize with a digital 3D model to provide direct spatial input.

GlimNavi combines proprietary AI models, 2D artwork, 3D information, physical interaction and editable intermediate results in one visual production environment, letting generative technology assist specific artistic decisions while creators retain control over the artwork.

55585.x: A wildfire is easiest to contain in the first minutes after it starts. The harder problem is knowing where it will travel next.
IntelliVIX Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Smart Communities at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for VIXA Wildfire AI, an integrated wildfire detection and spread-prediction platform.

Built on custom NPU hardware, the platform links edge AI, vision-language verification, spatial-temporal forecasting and autonomous drone sensing into one response workflow. Edge cameras run optimized YOLOv7/v9 models on NPU AI Boxes to spot smoke and flame within one kilometer.

To cut false alarms, an on-device vision-language model, Llama 3.2-3B, checks the visual evidence and writes natural-language incident reports; the description puts the reduction at 90 percent. Once a fire ignites, a spatial-temporal engine built on ConvLSTM and a graph neural network fuses video feeds, terrain elevation and wind data to predict how the fire will spread.

Long-endurance hybrid EO/IR drones, rated for more than 100 minutes of flight and carrying onboard NPUs, fly over the predicted fire perimeter and stream live aerial video that updates the spread model as conditions change. The combined picture is shown on a GIS command dashboard and pushed through municipal emergency networks to prompt evacuation.

55586.x: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy has mostly meant either a big hospital chamber or a soft, low-pressure wellness pod. A professional-grade chamber sized for one person sits between the two.
INTEROCEAN was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for GRAVITY, a personal hyperbaric oxygen therapy chamber.

Gravity is a single-user hyperbaric oxygen chamber designed to bridge the gap between large, facility-based systems and lower-pressure personal chambers used mainly for wellness. The chamber is pressurized with air while 100 percent medical-grade oxygen is delivered directly to the user through an independent breathing circuit, a separation that limits oxygen accumulation inside the chamber while enabling operation at pressures up to 3.0 ATA, with the pressure vessel proof-tested at 7 ATA.

A large front viewing window reduces the sense of enclosure and allows continuous observation by an operator during treatment, while automated pressure control and decompression reduce manual coordination for consistent supervised sessions.

Built on the same clinical engineering InterOcean has applied for 33 years to recompression chambers that treat divers with decompression sickness, Gravity is a professional-grade HBOT platform, not a mild hyperbaric wellness system, for single-user rehabilitation, sports recovery, wellness and other professionally managed applications.

55587.x: Many skin treatments force a choice between results and recovery time, trading downtime for effect. Getting both gentleness and depth out of one device is the difficulty.
Ion Medical Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Beauty Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for TheiDerm, a hybrid plasma-microwave non-invasive skin therapy platform.

The description calls TheiDerm the world's first hybrid plasma-microwave therapeutic platform, delivering continuous atmospheric plasma and microwave energy at once without harmful ozone, electrical arcing or thermal tissue damage. Its non-invasive approach increases skin permeability to boost absorption of therapeutic actives, and the description says its proprietary plasma discharge architecture, protected by two U.S. patents, differs from conventional plasma devices that trade off safety against effectiveness.

Combining non-thermal atmospheric plasma with microwave energy, it is used for skin regeneration, aesthetic treatment, inflammation control, and wound and scar management, non-invasively and with no downtime.

The description says it is cleared as a Class II medical device by Korea's MFDS (K-FDA), with a U.S. FDA 510(k) submission in progress, and has been validated in six peer-reviewed studies across human and veterinary applications.

55588.x: Designing a new flavor has long been the work of a handful of specialists, taking months and a small fortune. Turning a plain description into something you can sip would compress all of that.
Joomidang Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for PalateNova, an AI flavor studio.

PalateNova turns a one-sentence flavor request into a drink in under a minute, the description says, work it notes has required one of fewer than 600 master flavorists worldwide, up to 12 months and $350,000 per flavor. Its generative AI, the peer-reviewed Flavor Diffusion architecture (NAACL 2025), compiles the request into an exact recipe, and a countertop studio pours it from 16 food-grade flavor bases plus sugar and acid, metered at 0.25-microliter precision.

Where today's generative AI produces text and images, the description calls PalateNova the first system to carry a plain-language prompt through to a poured drink, refined in conversation over three to five tasting rounds.

Behind it are more than 30,000 proprietary chemical and sensory records, with 97 percent chemical-combination and 80 percent sensory-prediction accuracy, in one engine powering both the studio and a recipe-only cloud service; the description frames it as putting a flavor lab on any counter for the smaller brands shut out of professional flavor design.

55589.x: When an expert takes a vacation, transfers or retires, the way they actually think usually leaves with them, and the handover notes never quite capture it. Making that knowledge something that can be passed on, merged and asked questions is a different kind of record.
KMSLab was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for K-Portal BrainWeave, an AI knowledge platform.

K-Portal BrainWeave is an AI knowledge platform that turns every employee's daily work records into a personal Second Brain and, for the first time, lets that brain be transferred, merged and queried collectively. It frames the problem as organizations watching expertise walk out the door with vacations, transfers and retirements, while handover documents never capture how an expert actually thinks.

Employees simply work in a block-based collaborative editor while AI automatically extracts keywords, relationships and summaries into a searchable knowledge graph reflecting each person's role and context. One click shares that brain with a colleague, view-only for a vacation or a full merge for a resignation, without copying data and with instant revocation.

Merged brains become an organization's collective intelligence: in a twenty-thousand-employee company, for example, the CEO can question all the accumulated knowledge at once and receive grounded, cited answers, making organizational memory permanent, transferable and alive.

55591.x: The same lipstick can look different on two people because lips differ in color and surface. A shade picked from a shelf cannot account for that.
Kolmar Korea received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Beauty Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for ChromaFlow™ AI-Guided Personalized Cosmetic Manufacturing Platform for Diverse Lip Profiles.

ChromaFlow is a handheld digital cosmetic manufacturing system that measures each user's lip bio-optical profile, predicts the final on-lip result and manufactures a personalized lip formulation on demand. Multimodal optical sensing captures color and surface characteristics that cause the same cosmetic to appear differently across users.

A physics-informed AI converts these measurements into a Digital Lip Twin, predicts how a formulation will appear on the user's lips and performs inverse formulation to calculate the base-and-pigment ratios required for the selected target color and finish.

The device then translates this digital recipe into a physical cosmetic through nanoliter-scale piezo metering and precision microfluidic mixing, delivering the finished formulation through an integrated applicator.

By connecting measurement, prediction, formulation, manufacturing and application in one workflow, ChromaFlow is billed as moving personalized beauty beyond recommending existing shades or dispensing predefined recipes to real-time, user-specific cosmetic manufacturing.

55592.x: Treating a skin condition like vitiligo patch by patch, with the same dose everywhere, ignores how differently each spot responds. Mapping the skin and aiming only where it is needed makes the care gentler and more exact.
Kolmar Korea was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the LumiJet AI Precision Skin Therapeutics Platform.

LumiJet is a closed-loop embodied-AI platform built to make vitiligo care more selective and less invasive. At each session, it turns optical, photoacoustic, impedance and prior-response data into a patient-specific longitudinal 3D pigment map, distinguishing regions that need intervention from those improving or needing remeasurement.

Rather than applying uniform point-by-point treatment, a physics-informed AI model predicts how needle-free NanoJet delivery and light-triggered plasmonic release interact beneath the skin, then an AI planner creates a minimum-effective protocol that pairs each selected site with NanoJet settings and matched localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) conditions while limiting non-lesional exposure. A calibrated sensing-delivery coordinate system and real-time skin-landmark tracking translate the plan into guided device action, with independent safety controls gating execution and on-device AI keeping raw skin data local.
At later sessions, LumiJet compares the updated map with prior response and redirects intervention toward persistent regions, making care more selective as the skin changes.

55598.cap: NEWJAK won four CES Innovation Awards from 2025 to 2027 for X-RUNNER (Content & Entertainment, Metaverse, 2025), SPORTRACK (XR & Spatial Computing, 2026), and SPACEON (Artificial Intelligence, 2027). | Image Provided by NEWJAK

55598.x: Spatial extended reality (XR) technology enterprise NEWJAK Co., Ltd. (CEO Haehyun Jung) announced that its proprietary Autonomous Spatial Intelligence Platform, SPACEON, has been named a CES Innovation Awards 2027 Honoree in the Artificial Intelligence category by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). The recognition marks the company’s third consecutive year of accolades at the world's largest technology exhibition, bringing its cumulative total to four CES Innovation Awards following dual honors for X-RUNNER in 2025 across Content & Entertainment and Metaverse, and recognition for SPORTRACK in 2026 within XR & Spatial Computing.

The achievement comes amid record competition, with CTA evaluating nearly 4,000 entries across 37 product categories for CES 2027—a 10% overall increase in submissions, led by a 15% surge in the Artificial Intelligence field. Departing from conventional XR systems that require participants to wear bulky headsets, external sensors, or handheld controllers, SPACEON transforms physical architectural spaces into autonomous environments that perceive, interpret, and adapt dynamically to human presence.

55598.cap: Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK | Image Provided by NEWJAK

55598.x: Developed in 2026, SPACEON operates via five integrated artificial intelligence modules: SENSE, MODEL, ADAPT, SYNC, and LEARN. Utilizing a LiDAR sensor array paired with a real-time Unreal Engine 5 rendering pipeline, the system tracks up to 15 individuals simultaneously across a 50-square-meter footprint without markers, maintaining a positional accuracy of ±3 cm. The platform completes AI inference in 30 milliseconds and achieves an end-to-end sensing-to-response latency of 48.2 milliseconds. This enables instant content calibration based on individual user profiles. For instance, when detecting a child with a shorter reach and slower reaction times, the platform automatically enlarges interactive targets by 35%, contracts the active interaction perimeter by 25%, and reduces game speed by 20%, assigning distinct roles and objectives to different participants who share the same room.

Engineered as a foundational operating infrastructure rather than single-use content, SPACEON allows multipurpose venue utilization where educational modules, media art exhibitions, retail showrooms, drone training simulations, and gaming formats run seamlessly on shared projection and compute hardware. The underlying architecture was developed through five major South Korean national R&D projects, including the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ Super-Gap Startup Project, the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) talent initiatives, and global cooperative R&D programs under the Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs (TIPA). NEWJAK holds registered patents in the United States, Japan, and China, has received a grant decision in Europe, and has filed a PCT international patent application for SPACEON.

55598.cap: Promotional banner for NEWJAK's SPACEON | Image Provided by NEWJAK

55598.x: The enterprise has demonstrated widespread operational reliability across South Korean defense, municipal, and educational facilities, deploying device-free XR installations at the Korea Army Training Center, Jihyo Elementary School in Goyang, the Chuncheon Idea Library, and the Hanam Mental Health Welfare Center, as well as a 20-school educational rollout across Incheon. In international markets, NEWJAK captured the Smart Glasses Core Technology Innovation Award of the Year for SPORTRACK at the Shenzhen International AI+AR Smart Glasses Industry Expo 2026 in China and executed an MOU with UAE-based MetaLife Metaverse for Middle Eastern expansion.

NEWJAK will present live demonstrations of SPACEON at CES 2027, from January 6 to 9, at the Venetian Expo, Halls A-D (Booth 50765), as part of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City Pavilion. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK, stated that SPACEON marks a transition from device-centric XR toward human-centric spatial intelligence where environments perceive and respond to human behavior, noting that the enterprise will actively leverage its third consecutive CES honor to scale licensing and distribution partnerships across educational, cultural, and commercial venue operators throughout North America and Europe.

55600.x: COCELO Co., Ltd., led by CEO Jaehyung Cho, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Gwangmyeong City pavilion, to introduce a wheeled quadruped platform for unmanned patrol and inspection of industrial facilities, along with a humanoid platform and related control technology it is developing for inspection and welding work.

The company will be at the Venetian Expo (Halls A-D, Booth 50423). COCELO builds robot platforms and AI-based control software for unmanned inspection and task automation at industrial sites. Its main applications are autonomous patrol and equipment inspection with the quadruped robot and inspection and welding with the humanoid. The company's core strength is development capability that links mechanical design, walking and driving control, autonomous driving, sensor integration and task motion generation.

The quadruped combines the movement efficiency of wheels with the terrain handling of legs, and the company is developing it to move through industrial facilities and collect data. For the humanoid, COCELO is working on posture adjustment by work position and coordination between the arms and upper body so the robot can carry out inspection and welding. Data collected in the field is used to improve the robots' perception and control, and actual operating requirements feed back into product upgrades.

COCELO is running paid proof-of-concept (PoC) projects in robotics with large corporations, mid-sized companies and public enterprises to test site requirements and how well robots fit. Its main PoC directions are welding robot development, quadruped-based automation of leak detection and humanoid development. For patrol and inspection, the team is reviewing movement methods and sensor configurations suited to each site, and for the humanoid it is defining postures and arm motions by workspace and target. The company is focused on turning functions validated in the field into follow-on deployments and continuous operation.

Its differentiator is the ability to combine locomotion structure, sensors, work tools and control software to match site conditions and the purpose of the task. COCELO wants to widen the scope in stages, from collecting information during patrols to approaching a work target to carry out inspection and welding. At CES 2027, it aims to find customers with real adoption demand and demonstration projects, and to secure co-development and paid PoC opportunities with sensor, welding equipment and process technology companies and system integrators.

Overseas expansion is under review for unmanned patrol and inspection and for welding automation in industrial facilities, and COCELO plans to choose its first target countries after weighing customer demand, field demonstration opportunities and technical support conditions. It is seeking facility operation and maintenance companies, industrial sensor and welding equipment specialists, and robot system integrators, particularly partners that can handle local customer development, installation, training and after-sales care. COCELO would start with initial demonstrations with such partners and expand on the basis of proven cases.

On the product side, the company plans to improve the stability of autonomous movement, repeated patrols and sensor data collection on the quadruped, and to verify posture holding, inspection motions, welding path tracking and work equipment integration on the humanoid in stages. COCELO's main challenges are securing movement stability and inspection reliability across varied site conditions and turning the robot's motions into actual weld quality and productivity. It is seeking links to demonstration spaces and demand companies, cooperation with inspection and welding process experts, and support for quality evaluation and safety verification, and it is also considering overseas certification and testing and local technical support partners.
