55601.x: EZSYS CO. LTD, led by CEO Herrick Oh, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Gwangmyeong City pavilion, to present ID-ARM, a biometric enrollment device for National ID, and ID-LINK, a multimodal identity authentication terminal.

The company will be at Venetian Eureka Park, Booth 50423_036. India and several African countries are moving past conventional ID systems to biometric digital identification, a shift EZSYS compares to the leap from fixed-line telephony to mobile networks.

EZSYS develops and supplies iris recognition software and biometric enrollment and authentication devices. For national identity (National ID) programs, it has developed and mass-produced iris enrollment and authentication equipment with biometric extraction and matching and presentation attack detection (PAD). Its main business base is India's Aadhaar, which has enrolled about 1.4 billion people according to the company, and digital ID programs built on MOSIP, the platform adopted by several African countries, where systems are still being built. The company supplies devices and its own software to these programs and says it is the only Korean company taking part with its own software and devices.

The company's new software package was listed in the NIST IREX 10 results in February 2026, and EZSYS is using the listing to expand National ID work based on its own software. IriUniverse One and IriUniverse Two, along with the related software package, have obtained India's STQC certification and passed MOSIP compatibility, which ties into African national ID programs. EZSYS has manufactured and exported a cumulative 500,000 iris devices, most of them used as digital ID in those countries.

ID-ARM is a biometric enrollment device for National ID that combines facial imaging, dual-iris enrollment, contactless fingerprint recognition and ID card and document reading in one device. Automatic tilt and tracking adjust to the user's position. The aim is to simplify installation and operating procedures compared with arrangements that need several separate devices.

ID-LINK is a multimodal identity authentication terminal that combines face, iris and contactless fingerprint recognition and links to a user's smartphone or other personal device through NFC. Instead of storing biometric credentials in a central database, it is designed to keep them securely on the personal device, which reduces the system-building burden and the privacy risks of concentrated storage in digital ticketing, access control and membership management. Using a mobile device as a digital ID, it is designed to block cloned or forged devices, access by unregistered users and spoofed biometric data. Depending on a service's security policy, the factors can be selected or combined to set different authentication security levels.

EZSYS currently exports to India and several African countries and aims to widen its applications with multimodal products built for growing demand for integrated biometric devices. The company says ID-LINK addresses the database-building and management complexity and the legal issues that have burdened biometric authentication, because verification happens on the mobile device.

EZSYS recently built contactless fingerprint recognition into its iris products. India's STQC certification is the key requirement for iris products and U.S. NIST certification for fingerprints, and new products must obtain them. The costs run from about USD 30,000 at the low end to USD 100,000 to USD 300,000 at the high end, a heavy burden for a small company. Government support currently covers general certifications such as CE and UL but not these specialized ones, and the company said that covering them would help considerably.

55602.x: Waiting for elevators and hoists is a cost in itself on high-rise construction sites. In its own analysis, GoLe Robotics found that losses from this waiting amounted to about 19% of total labor costs, and a simulation of a 2,000-household apartment project showed that material-transport robots could shorten the schedule by about one month.

GoLe Robotics Co., Ltd., led by CEO Dongmin Lee, will present ND-1, a heavy-material transport robot, and EVW-2, an elevator-integration robot, at CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas. ND-1 was named a CES 2027 Innovation Awards Honoree in the Robotics category.

ND-1 carries up to 300 kilograms on its own, and two units working in sync move pipes 3 to 6 meters long without cutting them. EVW-2 presses elevator buttons physically, so robots can change floors without any modification to the elevator. Rather than take a humanoid form, ND-1 is built around the dimensions of elevator cars, narrow corridors and standard doorways. It lifts materials inside its own frame, without a mast or hydraulics, and runs a vision-language-action (VLA) model onboard to recognize material type and stacking direction without barcodes. The robot navigates autonomously in basements and shafts where communications drop and runs up to 10 hours on a single charge. Used together, ND-1 and EVW-2 make round-the-clock site logistics possible: delivering materials to work areas overnight and carrying waste out on the return trip.

Founded in 2023, GoLe Robotics develops autonomous robots for construction sites and focuses on automating material transport. The company was started by a construction engineer with more than 13 years of field experience at a major Korean contractor. Besides ND-1, its lineup includes GL-1 for finishing materials in apartment construction, GT-3 for 1-ton loads in industrial plants and the EVW series of elevator-integration robots. All of the robots share a common driving platform with task-specific modules, so configurations can be changed to suit site conditions. Its core strength is on-device AI that keeps working where connectivity drops, including semiconductor and data center sites where security rules restrict cloud use; the robots recognize materials and navigate on onboard computing alone. GoLe Robotics is a member of NVIDIA Inception and carries out a national construction-robot R&D project for Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

The company has operated material-transport robots on apartment and industrial-plant construction sites and has completed a pilot of autonomous transport robots on a semiconductor fab construction site in Korea. It won CES 2026 Innovation Awards before this year's Robotics honor, making 2027 its second consecutive year of awards. In 2026, it was selected for the Smart Construction Technology Demonstration program run by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology, and it appears in Startup Alliance's 2026 Physical AI Startup Map as an autonomous-driving company in construction and infrastructure. In June, it presented its construction physical AI technology at the Startup Day of NVIDIA GTC Taipei 2026 and signed a memorandum of understanding with MetAI, a Taiwanese digital twin company. In November, it presented at Physical AI Startup Connect during NVIDIA AI Day Seoul 2026.

GoLe Robotics has no formal export sales yet. It has set up a U.S. entity in Delaware as groundwork for overseas expansion. The United States is its first target market: with AI data centers and semiconductor fabs being built at the same time, construction labor is scarce and costly, and the company sees the greatest payoff there from automating material transport. It aims to begin selling the EVW series in the United States in 2027 after U.S. certification and to pursue on-site pilots of ND-1 at U.S. data center and semiconductor projects. Taiwan, where fab construction is active, is its second market, and the company also plans to enter overseas markets alongside Korean contractors on their international projects. It is looking for general contractors and engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies building data centers and fabs that can host site pilots, local construction-equipment rental and distribution companies with field support staff, and elevator and vertical-transport installation and maintenance companies. In Korea, GoLe Robotics plans to extend its robots to large sites such as semiconductor plants and AI data centers in 2027.

Its main challenges are the cost and lead time of overseas certification, since deploying robots on U.S. sites requires electrical and safety certification that is a heavy burden for a startup, and the difficulty of securing pilot sites without a local network, given strict site access and security procedures. Recruiting staff to operate and maintain the robots locally is a third. The company is seeking funding for overseas certification, matching with overseas contractors and project owners for site pilots, and programs that link startups to Korean contractors' overseas projects.

55603.x: in10sLab Co., Ltd., led by CEO Jiyoung Yoon, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Korean Venture Capital Association pavilion, to present Scailout Station, a tabletop conversation recorder that sits on the meeting table at a trade show booth.

The company will be at Venetian Eureka Park, Booth 62401. Scailout Station records the conversations at a booth and automatically produces a summary, a lead score and a follow-up email draft, which flow straight into lead management in Scailout, the company's global sales service. Staff do not have to wear the device or press a button, so the conversation is not interrupted. 55636.x: Manual wheelchair users feel every slope and uneven patch of ground through the seat. Staying level on terrain that tilts is a daily problem.
AIM Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for CENTRA.

CENTRA is an active stability module for manual wheelchairs. It mounts between the wheelchair frame and a side-mounted power-assist wheel using two tool-free adapters, and installs in about five minutes without modifying the chair. The adapters fit frame tubes from 19 to 25 mm, covering most manual wheelchair models.

An IMU, load cell and rotary encoder track the chair's pitch and roll. When terrain moves the center of gravity toward the edge of the support base, a motor-driven crank repositions each drive wheel relative to the frame, changing the wheelbase so the seat stays close to level.

Left and right cranks are driven independently, so the module responds to cross-slopes as well as inclines and obstacles. Correction runs without user input, and manual override remains available at all times.
The same sensors record vibration, shock and gradient along the route traveled, which the companion application uses to map surface hazards.

55638.x: A proper 3D look at how someone walks has meant a lab full of cameras, markers taped to the body and a specialist's week of work. So most people get judged by eye, and only after something has already gone wrong.
AIT Studio Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MEDISTEP M Pro 3D, a markerless 3D gait analysis system.

MEDISTEP M Pro 3D is a markerless 3D gait analysis system that runs on two tablets, standing in for a $300,000 optical motion-capture laboratory. Until now, an objective 3D gait assessment meant markers taped to the body, a dedicated room, a specialist and about a week of processing, which is why clinicians normally judge walking by eye and most people are first measured only after a fall or injury.

Placed at the front and side of the walking path, its two units record one short walk and fuse both views into a 19-joint 3D skeleton and a full gait report in about a minute, each showing 95 percent average agreement with gold-standard systems such as Vicon, Qualisys and GAITRite.
Any nurse, therapist or caregiver can run it, with no markers, no specialist and no internet, toward making 3D gait analysis a routine check wherever care happens.

55639.x: Changes in mood and memory often begin quietly. Noticing them early gives people more options.
Algocare was named a 2027 Honoree in two categories, Accessibility & Longevity and Artificial Intelligence, at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for algoMind.

algoMind transforms an everyday supplement dispenser into an on-device AI mental health coach that detects early signs of depression and cognitive decline, including dementia and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). On the dispenser's touchscreen tablet, users report how they feel that day, and the device instantly blends a personalized supplement combination.

In that brief moment, as the camera reads the face, a voice conversation guides the blend and fingers tap the screen, algoMind captures physical and psychological state from facial expressions, mental state from the voice and cognitive state from touch patterns. It combines these signals with health checkup records, prescription data and everyday usage patterns to infer the user's overall mental state and identify early signals of depression and MCI.

All analysis runs in a secure on-device environment where personal data never leaves the device. algoMind then adjusts supplement combinations and connects users to cognitive behavioral therapy through its mobile app.

55640.x: Moving a digital asset comes down to one signing step, and whatever asks for that signature is trusted to be legitimate. An attacker who reaches that moment can move funds as if they were the owner.
ANAM145 received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Cybersecurity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SignTrail, a pre-signing security control layer for digital-asset signing infrastructure.

SignTrail is deployed in front of signers such as HSMs, MPC systems, custody platforms and application or node signing services. At the moment of signing, the description says it verifies whether a blockchain transaction request came from a trusted execution path with its designated code, configuration and other files unmodified, binding the transaction payload, the request's runtime provenance, the policy context and the signer identity into a single signed decision checked immediately before the signing operation runs.
If the execution path or designated files fail verification, the signing operation is blocked and the system fails closed, and every decision is recorded as verifiable, hash-chained evidence.

Unlike key-protection or transaction-screening tools, the description says SignTrail treats runtime provenance as a required condition for signing authorization; it runs on the customer's own infrastructure and never receives or accesses private keys.

Anamofit is an integrated AI-based video content production tool for media wall displays. Traditional media wall production requires extensive manual optimization for each unique site, a process that is both costly and time-consuming.

Anamofit addresses this by integrating generative AI for asset creation, including 3D models, animations and backgrounds, with automated site-specific distortion correction. This enables scalable production of immersive 3D anamorphic visual experiences across displays with diverse shapes, sizes, curvatures and resolutions.

By unifying scene generation, display environment modeling, content adaptation, visual inspection and final output in a single AI-driven workflow, Anamofit dramatically reduces production time and cost. Its technical validity and real-world applicability are being validated through deployment on a 17-meter circular media wall installation at Jeju Folk Village, Republic of Korea.

55642.x: Medical imaging usually happens in a room built for it. Some patients cannot easily get to that room.
POSKOM Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Imaging at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for AirRay-micro.

AirRay-micro is billed as the world's lightest and smallest ultra-portable diagnostic X-ray system, designed to bring X-ray capability directly to locations where conventional imaging equipment is difficult to deploy.

MicroCore integrates X-ray generation, battery power, electronics and on-device control into a 1.5 kg (3.3 lbs) unit that healthcare professionals can carry and position directly at the patient. AutoRange uses laser distance sensing to detect changes in source-to-patient distance and support exposure control during repositioning. RapidLung AI analyzes chest X-rays for nine major pulmonary diseases within three seconds with over 96% accuracy.

These three technologies support rapid X-ray deployment, distance-aware exposure control and pulmonary analysis in bedside care, emergency response, home healthcare, mobile clinics and other locations where conventional X-ray equipment is difficult to deploy.

55646.cap: Jongwoo Jung, CEO of CITYEYELAB | Photo - AVING News

55646.x: Cities and expressways with advanced transportation infrastructure already have a large number of CCTV cameras, but most of them remain one-way monitoring tools that control-room operators check with their own eyes. Measuring accurate traffic volume and vehicle types has also meant burying detectors (VDS/AVC) or sending surveyors onto the road, which brings heavy road-surface construction costs, lane closures and on-site safety risks. CITYEYELAB, a deep-tech startup founded in Pangyo in January 2021, overcomes these limits by using AI to analyze footage from CCTV cameras already installed on existing roads.

CITYEYELAB developed CITY.EYE, an AI video analytics solution, based on its vision of "One Platform, Any Video Source, All Mobility Tasks." Conventional video analytics relied on single-image capture and struggled to recognize vehicles that overlap or appear at night or in bad weather. CITYEYELAB instead introduced trajectory-based analysis, which tracks each vehicle from the moment it enters the frame until it leaves. It also applies patented 3D geometric calibration to correct distortion caused by differences in camera height and angle, and derives vehicle position and speed along with detailed 6-class and 12-class vehicle classification.

The technology was proven through the Korea Expressway Corporation's AI-based Traffic Survey and Verification System project. Using footage from about 9,500 CCTV cameras installed on expressways nationwide, CITYEYELAB successfully delivered a system that automatically produces 12-class vehicle classification, traffic volume and speed, and it achieved stable accuracy of 95% or higher across diverse road environments. The system also lets users verify output data by checking it directly against the source footage, which substantially raises data reliability.

CITYEYELAB continues to expand its portfolio with CITY.SIGNAL, a signal optimization simulation solution; CITY.AV, an infrastructure-cooperative dynamic traffic information platform demonstrated at the intersection north of Pangyo Station and with the Panta-G Bus (Pangyo's autonomous shuttle bus); and CITY.SAFE, an early electric vehicle fire detection platform. In B2G, the technology serves road management agencies and local governments for traffic policy and public procurement. In B2B, it is expanding to engineering firms that conduct traffic impact assessments, drive-through and large-building commercial area analysis, system integration (SI) companies for control systems, and CCTV and edge equipment makers.

55646.cap: Turning 9,500 Expressway Cameras Into Smart AI Traffic Sensors! | CITYEYELAB Interview

55646.x: For overseas expansion, the company plans to open markets through technology partnerships with local traffic engineering firms and SI companies. Its platform can extract traffic data simply by uploading existing CCTV footage, with no separate road-surface sensors or electromagnetic detector construction. CITYEYELAB is currently seeking Pre-Series A investment. It plans to step up its participation in overseas city-related exhibitions from 2027 and to look for global partners, with the goal of attending CES 2028.

AVING News met with CITYEYELAB CEO Jongwoo Jung in Pangyo Techno Valley to discuss CITY.EYE, the AI traffic survey solution that turns the 9,500 CCTV cameras already installed along Korean expressways into traffic sensors, how CITY.SIGNAL and CITY.AV take video analytics from recognition to action, how the company plans to take its platform overseas through partners, and what Pangyo offers a company like CITYEYELAB.
Q1. Please introduce CITYEYELAB.

A. CITYEYELAB, as the name suggests, is a company that acts as the eyes of the city. Our mission is "One Platform, Any Video Source, All Mobility Tasks." In line with that mission, we connect the CCTV cameras across a city and use their footage to generate a range of traffic information.
Q2. How does your technology use the CCTV cameras that are already installed?

A. A single intersection in a city can have six to seven CCTV cameras, and sometimes as many as 10. Most existing CCTV is used for control: operators in a control center watch the footage. As AI has advanced, we have developed AI video-analytics technology that works with existing control CCTV as it is. Once the footage reaches the control center, AI can run on it there, so there is no need to add AI at the camera site.
Q3. What is your flagship solution, and where has it been applied?

A. Our flagship solution is CITY.EYE, an AI traffic survey solution. Our main deployment is with the Korea Expressway Corporation, where 9,500 CCTV cameras are already installed along Korean expressways. Until now, those cameras have been used mostly for control. People watched the footage to judge whether traffic was congested or flowing, or whether an accident had occurred. With our system, traffic information is generated automatically from the CCTV footage.
Q4. Where do you want to take this next?
A. We want to build a system in which control CCTV automatically recognizes and assesses accidents, safety issues and road conditions such as potholes, and alerts control-room operators in advance.
Q5. What other solutions do you offer beyond traffic surveys?

A. Through video analytics, we keep building mobility systems that go beyond simple recognition to action. CITY.SIGNAL is a signal optimization solution. It generates traffic information from city intersections, simulates how traffic signals should be operated based on that information, and verifies the effect. CITY.AV provides dynamic traffic information for cooperative autonomous driving. We are using it to give the Panta-G Bus (Pangyo's autonomous shuttle bus) infrastructure-level traffic information in the form of a 3D map.
Q6. Who uses your solutions?

A. Our customers fall into private and public sectors. In the private sector, most are engineering firms. When they build a building or widen a road, they have to survey how the traffic environment will change before and after, and that requires traffic information. We produce that traffic information and deliver the data. Drive-through stores are another example. When they or other buildings are planned, the traffic volume and foot traffic around the site have to be analyzed, and our system is used for that as well.

In the public sector, our solutions are used mainly when setting traffic operation policy. Korea conducts a traffic survey every October, and the United States, Europe and other Asian countries conduct one about once a year or about once a month. Our services are used for those surveys.
Q7. Why are you building a platform, and how does it help you expand overseas?

A. We are building a platform because our goal is to export. As I mentioned, public and private organizations abroad also need to collect traffic information in the same way as in Korea. In overseas cases, traffic surveys have mostly relied on electromagnetic sensors installed under the road. With our platform, traffic information can be generated simply by uploading recorded video. So we aim to build the platform and open it to overseas markets.
Q8. Do you have overseas cases, and how will you enter overseas markets?

A. We do not have specific overseas cases yet. But we have built a track record in Korea, and in particular we won a large public agency, the Korea Expressway Corporation, as a customer and delivered the system. As we expand abroad, we plan to present our domestic portfolio to overseas customers. We cannot go overseas directly, so we will work through overseas partners. If partners use our platform, they can apply it abroad right away, so we expect it to be a business that is easy to adopt.
Q9. What are your short-term plans?

A. In the short term, we aim to attend CES 2028. We also plan to take part in city-related exhibitions in Korea and abroad. Starting in 2027, we will use exhibitions to recruit partners for the platform we are completing this year.
Q10. What are the advantages of being based in Pangyo?

A. Pangyo has a high concentration of IT companies, so it offers a lot of support for IT firms. For a company like ours, demonstration on real roads is especially important. We ran the demonstration of CITY.AV communicating with the Panta-G Bus here in Pangyo, and the field demonstration of CITY.SIGNAL signal optimization here as well. Pangyo is IT-friendly and has many job seekers who want to work in IT, so it is also a very good place for an IT company to find new colleagues.

55653.x: In heavy smoke and a blackout, a fixed exit sign is useless the moment it disappears from view, and an announcement cannot say which way is still safe. A light that flies ahead and leads people out answers the question in real time.
LEADWAY and Hanseo University received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Smart Communities at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for LEADWAY, an autonomous dynamic evacuation guidance system.

LEADWAY replaces static exit signs with autonomous drones that fly ahead of evacuees and physically lead them out. Units patrol continuously, so the drone that first identifies a fire signals standby units to deploy across the building within seconds, where in heavy smoke and power outages fixed signage and building-wide announcements cannot tell anyone which way is still safe.

It uses high-visibility directional lighting as the primary cue, extending the visible route from 1 to 8 meters and raising route recognition from 46 percent to 91 percent, with onboard voice guidance as a supporting layer. Thermal and vision sensors locate stranded occupants and re-route crowds away from compromised exits, while a mesh network keeps every unit and arriving first responders on one live picture.
Across offices, residential buildings, transit hubs and schools, LEADWAY targets a drop in evacuation time from 12 to 7 minutes.

55654.x: A burning electric car in an enclosed parking garage is hard to put out and dangerous to approach. Firefighters face heat, toxic gas and the risk of an explosion.
Lee mobility Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Robotics at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the EV Fire Defense Robot, an autonomous direct-to-battery cooling and fire suppression robot.

The EV Fire Defense Robot is an autonomous firefighting robot designed to suppress thermal runaway within electric vehicle battery packs. It autonomously approaches the vehicle, positions itself beneath the battery and deploys a compact module equipped with an alloy penetration nozzle.

Using an electro-hydraulic mechanism, the nozzle penetrates the battery casing and sprays extinguishing fluid directly onto the battery pack. This direct spraying method enables rapid suppression, reduces the risk of re-ignition and minimizes water consumption and contaminated spills.
Supporting both autonomous and remote operation, the robot protects firefighters from heat, toxic gases and explosion hazards in enclosed environments such as parking lots or charging stations.

55655.x: Solar power usually arrives as rigid panels bolted to a roof, which limits where it can go. Anything curved, small or indoors has mostly been left out.
LEECELL Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Energy Transition & Sustainability at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SOLWEAR: The Solar Roll.

SOLWEAR is a flexible thin-film solar cell made as a continuous roll using a proprietary ambient-pressure roll-to-roll wet-coating process, which the description says allows extensive length scalability and lowers manufacturing costs compared with vacuum deposition. Mass-produced rolls deliver over 10 percent efficiency under standard sunlight and over 20 percent in indoor low-light environments.

The film works as an adaptable power source: it can be custom-cut in multiple directions to fit various surface shapes, and its material formulation enables tunable light transmittance for transparent applications.
SOLWEAR powers indoor IoT sensors and electronic shelf labels, while its flexibility supports structural integration into building exteriors (BIPV), mobility (MIPV) and smart agriculture (APV).

55656.x: People read much of a conversation from the face. Expression is how we sense whether someone is listening.
LG Display was named a 2027 Honoree in Robotics at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for 8-inch Light Field Display (Humanoid Face).

LG Display's Light Field Display (LFD) is billed as the world's first 3D display solution specifically designed for a humanoid face. Moving beyond the limitations of physically fixed robot face designs, its 3D optical technology creates lifelike visuals that enable more natural expression and emotional interaction between human and humanoid.
Without requiring any physical modification to the robot, the display can present a wide range of 3D facial expressions, virtual avatars and other user interfaces.

This flexibility expands the versatility of multi-purpose humanoids and enables a more immersive physical AI experience. By providing intuitive and natural communication, Light Field Display supports a humanoid-friendly environment for humans.

55657.x: On a sprawling construction or shipbuilding site, nothing stays where the plan said it would, so tracking what is actually built is a daily guess. Reading the real site as live data, instead of scanning barcodes, is a different way to know.
LiOps Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for LiOps Spatial MES, a live operating layer for industrial sites.

LiOps Spatial MES is a two-layer platform that turns ever-changing industrial sites into live, machine-readable operating data and puts robots to work on it. The sensing layer replaces the barcode: proprietary fixed-LiDAR scanning and GPU-accelerated deep learning make CAD registration hundreds of times faster than conventional ICP, automatically identifying every workpiece and measuring per-part assembly progress in real time, feeding actuals into existing ERP/MES with zero site preparation.

At the execution layer, autonomous robot welding crews operate on the same coordinates, performing unstructured welding with zero jigs, teaching or fixed trajectories and billed strictly by completed output, as heavy industry has bought labor for decades. Each layer stands alone, and both are already sold under paid contracts.
The platform applies wherever large structures are built, including shipbuilding, EPC, plant, steel fabrication and offshore energy.

55658.x: Before a worker steps into a hazardous zone, someone has to be sure there is no fire, gas or intruder waiting there. Sending a machine in first to check and record the scene keeps people out of harm's way.
LK ROBOTICS Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for LKR-VisionX, an industrial safety orchestration system.

LKR-VisionX is an AI-native industrial safety system that unifies sensing, verification, decision-making and physical response on a single mobile platform. It integrates a motorized pan-and-tilt coaxial EO/IR head, four-direction around-view monitoring, LiDAR, and gas and acoustic sensing with on-device AI, and an onboard AI agent evaluates each event and converts the decision into Physical AI actions through the host platform.

Before workers enter a hazardous area, LKR-VisionX inspects the scene, verifies fire, gas, overheating, intrusion or dangerous proximity, and records structured evidence remotely. It then warns nearby workers, redirects the platform, restricts approach and escalates the event to the control room.
Its robot-agnostic design reduces blind spots, lowers integration cost and speeds response across multiple robot platforms.

55659.x: A teacher often has the raw material for a good lesson already, scattered across old slides, PDFs and recordings. Turning that pile into something students can work through is the part that eats the evening.
Makit AI Labs Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in EdTech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Makit AI Learning OS, a platform for building and running STEM classes.

Makit AI Learning OS is a browser-based platform for creating, running and analyzing technology and STEM classes. Instructors turn material they already have, including recorded lectures, PDFs, slides or video, or a single written instruction, into a lesson unit called a Capsule, which combines explanations, auto-graded questions, interactive simulations and runnable code exercises, and each generated unit stays linked to the timestamp of the source material it came from. Capsules are distributed by link or QR code and open on any browser, so students need no account and no installation.
During class, LiveBridge shows the instructor every learner's screen and progress at once, flags who has stalled or hit an error, and allows intervention on the learner's own screen.
After class, the system reports question-level accuracy and the misconceptions that recurred, which teachers use to plan the next session.

55660.x: Most waste plastic ends up burned or buried, and few people think of it as something that could feed soil. Turning it into a material a farm can use would change where that plastic goes.
MCE Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Construction & Industrial Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Eco-mealworm Lv2: Containerized Industrial System for On-Site Plastic Resource Recovery.

Eco-mealworm Lv2 is a containerized industrial system for on-site plastic resource recovery that reverses the flow of waste plastic, millions of tons of which are incinerated or landfilled every year. With no live insects involved, it runs a mealworm-gut-derived microbial consortium and enzyme system in industrial reactors to open the benzene rings of waste plastic and convert it into a humic substance that revitalizes soil.

In a 100 kg reactor, 40% of pretreated polystyrene is converted within 24 hours, and after 72 hours no residual polystyrene is detectable. Oxygen content rises from about 1% to 43% to 44%, indicating a hydrocarbon transformed into an oxygen-rich humic structure. The humic substance is now undergoing EU REACH registration.

Lv2 is the industrial evolution of Lv1, a CES 2025 Innovation Awards Honoree in which live mealworms consumed styrofoam, and it now scales without insect-rearing infrastructure. The process is designed for hi-cube container modules that install at waste-generating sites and scale out in parallel, returning plastic to farmland rather than to fuel oil.

55662.x: Medical students learn from flat textbook questions that rarely resemble the scans and cases they will face. Practicing inside a real image, or a model you can turn in your hands, is closer to the work.
MediCherry Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in EdTech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MyMerci Clinical Learning Intelligence, a platform for healthcare students and clinicians.

MyMerci Clinical Learning Intelligence is a web and mobile platform for healthcare students and practicing clinicians. Its questions combine exam blueprints, verified items, medical terminology and theory across 18 released interactive formats, and learners answer some items within real CT, MRI or X-ray studies or by rotating a licensed 3D anatomy model. The tutor withholds answers and asks students concept questions, while practitioners receive concise briefings.

Explanations retrieve biomedical literature and display numbered sources with confidence and review status, and before generated content reaches learners, deterministic checks screen for invalid answers and answer cues, independent models assess higher-risk items, and human reviewers control publication.

The same grounding and review pipeline serves Korean, English, Japanese, Traditional Chinese and Vietnamese content, and MyMerci is an educational platform, not a diagnostic, treatment or clinical decision-support tool.
